summary: Reentrant, cross-dialect unit-of-work machinery behind IbisBackend.transaction(). Keeps a module-level registry keyed on id(raw_handle) under a lock; the outermost scope decides ownership and nested scopes join flatly (no savepoints). On ownership dialects (sqlite, duckdb, postgres) entry probes native state to begin-and-own or join a caller's open transaction without completing it, and exit verifies commit eligibility. Caught failures poison the scope. Exposes is_active(), protection_required() and mark_poisoned() for the protection layer.
extension_points: Dialects participate through DialectSpec transaction fields (begin_statement, begin_hook, in_transaction_probe, precommit_probe, raw_execute_hook); OWNERSHIP_DIALECTS selects the ownership path
lifecycle_notes: Never toggles the driver's autocommit flag
Registers after BEGIN so a failed BEGIN leaves no stale entry
An ambiguous COMMIT failure is never retried; on_commit_failure discards owned connections
TransactionSupport.NONE raises TransactionUnsupportedError unless required=False, which warns once and no-ops
documentation_hooks: Why a native COMMIT through a raw escape hatch raises at scope exit
risks: Registry provides sequential reentrancy only, not cross-thread arbitration on one raw connection
Keyed on id(raw_handle): a freed handle's id could be reused, though entries are popped in finally
